"'''50 Ways to Leave Your Lover'''" is a song by the American singer-songwriter [[Paul Simon]]. It was the second [[Single (music)|single]] from his fourth studio album, ''[[Still Crazy After All These Years]]'' (1975), released on [[Columbia Records]]. Backing vocals on the single were performed by [[Patti Austin]], [[Valerie Simpson]], and [[Phoebe Snow]]. The song features a recognizable repeated drum riff performed by drummer [[Steve Gadd]].

One of his most popular singles, "50 Ways" was released in December 1975 and began to see chart success in the new year. It became Simon's sole [[Hot 100 number-one hits of 1976 (United States)|number-one hit]] as a solo artist on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] in the United States and was his highest-charting song in France, where it peaked at number two. Elsewhere, the song was a top 20 hit in Canada and New Zealand. The single was certified [[RIAA certification|gold]] by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA), denoting sales of more than one million copies.

An edit of the song that cuts out a few seconds of the intro is included on ''The Paul Simon Collection: On My Way, Don't Know Where I'm Goin'''.<ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?si=n-N-8qeTr_hdkUAs&v=2wmyjGrN7M0&feature=youtu.be |title=50 Ways To Leave Your Lover |date=2014-11-05 |last=Paul Simon – Topic |access-date=2024-12-27 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

"50 Ways to Leave Your Lover" is a song by the American singer-songwriter Paul Simon. It was the second single from his fourth studio album, Still Crazy After All These Years (1975), released on Columbia Records. Backing vocals on the single were performed by Patti Austin, Valerie Simpson, and Phoebe Snow. The song features a recognizable repeated drum riff performed by drummer Steve Gadd.

One of his most popular singles, "50 Ways" was released in December 1975 and began to see chart success in the new year. It became Simon's sole number-one hit as a solo artist on the Billboard Hot 100 in the United States and was his highest-charting song in France, where it peaked at number two. Elsewhere, the song was a top 20 hit in Canada and New Zealand. The single was certified gold by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA), denoting sales of more than one million copies.

An edit of the song that cuts out a few seconds of the intro is included on The Paul Simon Collection: On My Way, Don't Know Where I'm Goin.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
Following his divorce from his first wife Peggy Harper, Simon opted to take a more humorous approach to document the event.<ref>{{cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=August 23, 2019 |title=The Number Ones: Paul Simon's "50 Ways To Leave Your Lover" |url=https://www.stereogum.com/2055734/the-number-ones-paul-simons-50-ways-to-leave-your-lover/columns/the-number-ones/ |access-date=August 18, 2024 |website=Stereogum}}</ref> He recorded the song at [[A&R Recording]] on 48th Street in New York City,<ref name=Williams2023/> a small studio "in the heart of [[Broadway (Manhattan)|Broadway]]'s theater district", and built the song around percussion—"martial drums" in particular—in order to "avoid clutter".<ref>{{cite web |author=Anon. |date=2024 |orig-date=1996 |title=50 Ways to Leave Your Lover |url=https://www.superseventies.com/1976_9singles.html |website=SuperSeventies.com |access-date=April 7, 2019}}</ref> Simon described the song as "just a fluke hit that I slipped into by accident".<ref name="Number 1"/>

In 2023, Simon appeared on ''[[The Howard Stern Show]]'' and stated that he wrote the chorus lyrics while teaching his son Harper how to rhyme.<ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zwcouyvUpFc&ab_channel=TheHowardSternShow |title=Paul Simon on Writing “50 Ways to Leave Your Lover” |date=2023-09-22 |last=The Howard Stern Show |access-date=2025-01-09 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

[[Steve Gadd]] recalled that the drumbeat for "50 Ways to Leave Your Lover" was originally uniform across the verses and choruses, although at A&R Recording, both Simon and [[Phil Ramone]] asked Gadd to rework the verses with a different groove. In between takes, Gadd was quietly practicing drum patterns by placing particular emphasis on the [[hi-hat]] cymbal. Ramone overheard him practicing and asked him to incorporate these ideas into the verses, which was ultimately retained in the final mix.<ref name=Williams2023>{{cite web |last=Williams |first=Stuart |date=March 15, 2023|title=Steve Gadd on His Drum Intro to Paul Simon's 50 Ways to Leave Your Lover: "It was a Lucky Day for Me" |url=https://www.musicradar.com/news/steve-gadd-50-ways-to-leave-your-lover-drum-intro-paul-simon |access-date=August 18, 2024 |website=MusicRadar}}</ref>

It has been jokingly pointed out that although the song's title is "50 Ways to Leave Your Lover", the lyics reference only five unique methods.<ref>{{cite web |last=Leonetti |first=Michael |date=April 6, 2020 |title=The Other 45 Ways to Leave Your Lover That Paul Simon Didn't Want You to See |website=Points in Case |url=https://www.pointsincase.com/lists/the-other-45-ways-to-leave-your-lover-that-paul-simon-didnt-want-you-to-see |access-date=August 12, 2024}}</ref>
sections.text:
Following his divorce from his first wife Peggy Harper, Simon opted to take a more humorous approach to document the event. He recorded the song at A&R Recording on 48th Street in New York City, a small studio "in the heart of Broadway's theater district", and built the song around percussion—"martial drums" in particular—in order to "avoid clutter". Simon described the song as "just a fluke hit that I slipped into by accident".

In 2023, Simon appeared on The Howard Stern Show and stated that he wrote the chorus lyrics while teaching his son Harper how to rhyme.

Steve Gadd recalled that the drumbeat for "50 Ways to Leave Your Lover" was originally uniform across the verses and choruses, although at A&R Recording, both Simon and Phil Ramone asked Gadd to rework the verses with a different groove. In between takes, Gadd was quietly practicing drum patterns by placing particular emphasis on the hi-hat cymbal. Ramone overheard him practicing and asked him to incorporate these ideas into the verses, which was ultimately retained in the final mix.

It has been jokingly pointed out that although the song's title is "50 Ways to Leave Your Lover", the lyics reference only five unique methods.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
Contemporary reviews of "50 Ways to Leave Your Lover" were positive, with ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' calling it an "excellent song" that has "very clever lyrics" and an "easy to listen to melody".<ref name=bb>{{cite news|title=Top Single Picks|newspaper=Billboard|access-date=2020-07-13|date=December 13, 1975|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-Billboard/70s/1975/Billboard-1975-12-13.pdf|page=58}}</ref>  ''[[Cash Box]]'' said that it is "a clever, commercial song about the elasticity of love, how easy it is to pull away and equally easy to snap back with it."<ref name=cb>{{cite news|title=CashBox Singles Reviews|date=December 13, 1975|page=16|accessdate=2021-12-11|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Cash-Box/70s/1975/CB-1975-12-13.pdf|newspaper=Cash Box}}</ref> ''[[Record World]]'' said that the song "finds Simon aided by a crack team of session men and the unmistakable vocals of [[Phoebe Snow]]".<ref name=rw>{{cite magazine|magazine=Record World|date=December 13, 1975|accessdate=March 8, 2023|title=Hits of the Week|page=1|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Record-World/70s/75/RW-1975-12-13.pdf}}</ref><ref name=Eliot2010>{{cite book |page=142 |title=Paul Simon: A Life |author=Eliot, Marc |location = New York, NY | publisher=John Wiley and Sons |year=2010 |isbn=978-0-470-43363-8}}</ref>

''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' thought that Simon "reached a conversational, graceful peak on '50 Ways to Leave Your Lover'".<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Browne |first=David |date=January 18, 1991|title=Rating Paul Simon's albums |url=https://ew.com/article/1991/01/18/rating-paul-simons-albums/ |access-date=August 18, 2024 |magazine=Entertainment Weekly|language=en}}</ref> ''[[Spin (magazine)|Spin]]'' was more critical of the song and listed it as one of the "50 Worst Songs By Otherwise Great Artists".<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 20, 2022 |title=The 50 Worst Songs By Otherwise Great Artists |url=https://www.spin.com/2022/07/the-50-worst-songs-by-otherwise-great-artists/ |access-date=August 18, 2024 |website=Spin}}</ref>
sections.text:
Contemporary reviews of "50 Ways to Leave Your Lover" were positive, with Billboard calling it an "excellent song" that has "very clever lyrics" and an "easy to listen to melody".  Cash Box said that it is "a clever, commercial song about the elasticity of love, how easy it is to pull away and equally easy to snap back with it." Record World said that the song "finds Simon aided by a crack team of session men and the unmistakable vocals of Phoebe Snow".

Entertainment Weekly thought that Simon "reached a conversational, graceful peak on '50 Ways to Leave Your Lover'". Spin was more critical of the song and listed it as one of the "50 Worst Songs By Otherwise Great Artists".
